newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks perk up, market optimistic.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks perk up, market optimistic.

text.p: Croatian stocks perked up in robust trade on Tuesday two days after President Franjo Tudjman secured his second term in office, and traders foresaw slight gains and more optimism on the market.
"I think that the market is slowly recovering. Drugs firm Pliva is rising in London, Zagrebacka Banka is stable but on large volumes," Nenad Pavletic of Auctor brokerage said.
He said this was most probably due to the end of the presidential election on June 15 in which Tudjman defeated his two opponents, winning over 61 percent of the votes.

Although traders described Tudjman's victory as "predictable" and believed that as such it would not have a wider impact on price movements, some said the prices would have fallen if the government had changed.

"Staying in power guarantees stability. It is a sort of confirmation of stability, regardless of the fact that Tudjman's victory was predictable. It will influence the behaviour of foreign investors," he said.
Traders said an international report which branded the election unfair would not damage market stability.
"Investors don't mind as long as the political situation is stable because they have no ambitions to get involved with politics," Pavletic said.
Of 17 active issues nine rose, four fell and four were flat. Volume balooned to 23,228 shares, turnover to 15.9 from 3.4 million kuna.

Most active stock Pliva sold 8,349 shares, adding 18 kuna to 480 after peaking at 484 kuna earlier in the session. On the London Stock Exchange, Pliva's 1/5 global depositary receipts (GDRs) opened at $16.25 and rose to $16.3 by the afternoon.
Zagrebacka's ordinaries were flat at 2,035 kuna on volume of 4,253 shares. Its 1/10 GDRs trading on Seaq International eased to $34 from opening at $34.025.
Nikolac said the election outcome could probably spur more buying of Zagrebacka and Pliva in London.
"All foreign markets eagerly await the signals to move in some direction. It can have an impact on our not too liquid stocks trading in London," he said.
Food processor Podravka ended flat at 288 kuna with 4,163 shares sold. Confectioner Kras rose 10 kuna to 417, with 1,580 shares sold.
Biggest gainer hotelier Istraturist firmed 10 kuna to 180, with 340 shares changing hands. Biggest decliner hotelier Arenaturist fell to 125 kuna from 140 late in May, selling 57 shares.
